entities.name: Ecgberht I of Northumbria
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ecgberht I of Northumbria was king of Northumbria from approximately 794 to 810 CE, marking a pivotal period in the region's history. 

During his reign, Ecgberht oversaw the construction of several fortifications, including the fort of Tynemouth, which served as a key stronghold against Viking raids. 

His rule also saw the expansion of Northumbrian trade and cultural exchange with neighboring kingdoms, including the Picts and the Scots. 

Despite his efforts to maintain Northumbrian independence, Ecgberht's kingdom eventually fell to the Viking invasion of 878 CE, leading to the establishment of the Danelaw. 

'Give me your kingdom, and your treasure, and I will leave you in peace,' Ecgberht allegedly told King Ælla of Northumbria, foreshadowing the eventual collapse of his kingdom.
